title: Opium, Trade and the Qing
dek: Of how Britain paid for its tea with Indian opium, went to war to keep selling it, and opened China to a century of foreign power.

panels.label: As Each Side Told It
panels.text: British officials spoke of free trade and equal diplomacy; Qing officials spoke of a poison smuggled in by barbarians who would not obey the law.

panels.label: Evidence Allows
panels.text: Both sides were defending money. Britain needed opium to pay for tea; the Qing needed silver and authority. Force decided the question, and the Qing…
